theater: 兩河下游基什與伊朗高原埃蘭

battle.name: 基什-埃蘭戰爭
battle.theater: 兩河下游基什與伊朗高原埃蘭
battle.brief: 公元前2900年前後，北巴比倫的基什聯盟與東方伊朗高原的埃蘭（一般考作阿拉塔）為石料與寶石開戰。戰事只靠《蘇美爾王表》殘片與《恩美爾卡爾與阿拉塔之王》史詩留下痕跡，最終捲入烏魯克王恩美爾卡爾的東征。兩軍步兵皆以銅矛為骨幹；史詩不記兵刃，本卡那件埃及長矛代表考古為此役補回的細節。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰的兩方，是北巴比倫平原上的基什城邦聯盟，與東方山地的埃蘭（Éran，蘇美爾文作 En-an-na-ta）。基什一方是以核心城加衛星城組成的聯盟：基什本城之外，烏爾、烏魯克、埃利都等城邦在聯盟框架內提供人手，首腦由王或總督（ensi）擔任，軍隊戰時臨時召集，沒有常備的職業軍。埃蘭一方是伊朗高原西南部、扎格羅斯山地的古老政權，一般考作與史詩中的阿拉塔（Aratta）同一，位於克爾基內河與迪茲河流域的高地峽谷一帶，與安珊山地相連，憑石料、礦物與山道屏障自守。基什聯盟的目標在史詩中被改寫成「貢賦」：索取青金石、金銀、加工好的石料與金屬工匠；埃蘭一方則要保住物產與隘口。埃蘭的具體位置至今沒有共識，蘇西安納、安珊、迪亞拉與土庫曼斯坦南部都有人提出，本條以蘇西安納為代表點。戰爭在史詩層面還有第三方：烏魯克與伊南娜的介入；埃利都的恩赫伽爾則被王表記為仲裁者。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the league of cities headed by Kish on the northern Babylonian plain, and the highland power of Eran (Éran, written in Sumerian as En-an-na-ta). The Kish side was a league built from a core city and its satellite towns: besides Kish itself, Ur, Uruk and Eridu supplied men within the framework of the league, its head being a king or an ensi (governor), and its host was levied in time of war with no standing professional force. The Eran side was an old polity in the south-west of the Iranian plateau, in the Zagros highlands, generally identified with Aratta of the epic, lying in the highland gorges of the Karkheh and Dez basins with the Anshan highlands beyond, and holding itself behind its stone, its minerals and its mountain passes. What Kish wanted is restated by the epic as tribute: lapis lazuli, gold and silver, worked stone and metalworkers. What Eran wanted was to keep its produce and its defiles. The precise location of Eran still has no consensus; Susiana, Anshan, the Diyala and southern Turkmenistan have all been proposed, and this entry takes Susiana as the representative point. At the level of the epic there is a third party as well, Uruk with the intervention of Inanna; and En-hegal of Eridu appears in the king list as the arbiter.
people: 關鍵人物大半只留下名號，沒有可核對的生平。烏魯克之王恩美爾卡爾（Enmerkar）是整場衝突的推動者：《恩美爾卡爾與阿拉塔之王》史詩以他為主角，他派遣信使越過「祖比山」、經蘇薩與安珊、翻越「五、六、七座山」抵達阿拉塔要求貢賦；史詩說他為準備一件華麗權杖花了十年，又因信使記不住口信而改用泥板書寫，於是這場戰爭同時成了書寫發明的傳說。阿拉塔之王在主篇中不具名，只以「阿拉塔之主」出現，續篇《恩美爾卡爾與恩蘇赫吉拉阿納》中則名為恩蘇赫吉拉阿納（En-suhgir-ana），此名與恩美爾卡爾同源；他自恃伊南娜也曾選中自己，拒絕臣服，改提議雙方各遣勇士單挑。埃利都總督恩赫伽爾（En-hegal）出現在《蘇美爾王表》殘片與「恩赫伽爾銘文」中，那兩處正是「基什與埃蘭之爭」一句話記載的來源，因此他是這場戰爭在書寫傳統裡的仲裁者。女神伊南娜由阿拉塔轉投烏魯克，是史詩用來解釋戰局逆轉的原因；風雨神伊什庫爾讓阿拉塔田生生出野麥與鷹嘴豆，使阿拉塔不必因缺糧而屈服；續篇中的哈馬茲巫師與那位把他丟進幼發拉底河的女智者，則是另一樁與東方有關的衝突留下的角色。
peopleEn: Most of the key figures survive only as names, without a life that can be checked. Enmerkar, king of Uruk, is the driving force of the whole conflict: the epic Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta makes him its protagonist, sending heralds over the Zubi mountains, past Susa and Anshan, across the 'five, six, seven' mountains to Aratta to demand tribute; the epic says he spent ten years preparing an ornate sceptre, and that, unable to trust the heralds to remember all his messages, he had recourse to writing on tablets, so that this war became at the same time the legend of the invention of writing. The lord of Aratta is unnamed in the main poem and appears only as the lord of Aratta; in the sequel Enmerkar and En-suhgir-ana he is called En-suhgir-ana, a name of the same root as Enmerkar. Proud that Inanna had chosen him in his turn, he refused submission and proposed instead that each side send a champion to single combat. En-hegal, ensi of Eridu, appears in a fragment of the Sumerian King List and in the so-called inscription of En-hegal, and it is those very texts that preserve the single clause about the 'conflict between Kish and Eran', which makes him the arbiter of this war within the written tradition. The transfer of Inanna's allegiance from Aratta to Uruk is the epic's way of explaining the reversal of the war; the storm god Ishkur made wild wheat and chickpea grow in Aratta's fields, so that Aratta would not have to yield for want of grain; and the sorcerer from Hamazi in the sequel, together with the wise woman who threw him into the Euphrates, belongs to a different quarrel with the east.
kits: 兵器卡上的是埃及長矛：早王朝時期把銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上的步兵長矛，形制約在公元前3200年前後，埃及人用它守住城垣缺口，也在失地之後用它收復。在這場戰爭裡，長矛的位置有兩層。史料層：史詩只寫大軍與神的安排，幾乎不記兵刃，這一役的兵器細節要靠考古與他處文物補回，卡面那件長矛正代表這種補位。形制層：沒有任何文字說埃及人參與了基什與埃蘭的爭端，但早王朝蘇美爾步兵的骨幹兵器同樣是銅矛——扁平矛頭、菱形截面、帶中脊，裝在木杆上，近身靠刺擊與橫掃，與埃及樣式屬同一技術世代。史詩本身幾乎不列兵器細節，它寫的是大軍、神的安排與象徵性的「巨大武器」，因此雙方裝備的細節主要靠考古比對：早王朝美索不達米亞聚落與墓葬出土的銅矛頭、銅斧（marru）、短柄銅斧、匕首、棒錘（nar）、石彈、弓與箭，以及柳條或皮革蒙皮的圓盾；銅斧是最重的打擊兵器，銅矛負責在拉開距離之後解決貼身戰。攻城方面用土壘、壕溝、梯與撞木，運輸靠人肩、畜力與河道船隻。這場戰爭的年代還沒有戰車，蘇美爾的車兵要到早王朝第三期才出現在戰場上。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Egyptian spear: an infantry spear of the Early Dynastic period with a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, a form of about 3200 BC, used by the Egyptians to hold the gaps in their fortification walls and, after losing ground, to recover it. In this war the spear holds two positions. On the level of the record: the epic writes of great hosts and of the dispositions of the gods and hardly notes any blade, so that the weapons of this campaign have to be supplied by archaeology and by finds from elsewhere, and the spear on the card stands for that act of supplementation. On the level of form: no text says that the Egyptians took part in the quarrel between Kish and Eran, but the backbone weapon of the Early Dynastic Sumerian infantry was likewise the copper spear, with a flattened head, a lozenge-shaped section and a central ridge, bound to a wooden shaft, used at close quarters for thrusting and sweeping, and belonging to the same technical generation as the Egyptian examples. The epic itself hardly lists any detail of weapons; it writes of great hosts, of the dispositions of the gods and of symbolic 'great weapons', so that the equipment of both sides has to be reconstructed by archaeological comparison: copper spearheads, copper axes (marru), short-handled axes, daggers, maces (nar), sling stones, bows and arrows from Early Dynastic settlements and burials in Mesopotamia, together with round shields of withes or covered in leather; the copper axe was the heaviest striking weapon, and the copper spear settled the business once the distance had been closed. For siege work the towns used earth banks, ditches, ladders and battering timbers, and transport was by human shoulder, animal draught and river craft. The age of this war still had no war chariots; the Sumerian chariot force does not appear on the battlefield until the third phase of the Early Dynastic period.
tactics: 史詩保存的戰法，是一套「先外交、後野戰、再以水利收尾」的流程。第一步是連番派使：信使帶著口信與泥板往返，條件從大麥加寶石，一路加到金銀、銅礦（kugmea）、加工金屬與金屬匠人、加工石材與石匠，還有鑄模；阿拉塔一方一面拖延，一面提出替代方案，把衝突從臣服改成交易。第二步轉入武力：烏魯克與盟軍集結大軍，向東越過祖比山與安珊山地，在通向阿拉塔的河谷平原上列陣對峙；史詩形容對陣的阿拉塔軍隊如蠍子、如飛鳥，裝束奇異，義在顯示遠方軍隊的陌生與可怖，而不是可供考古還原的編制。第三步是決定性的一擊：以開渠引水把河水源引進平原，淹沒對軍陣地——這是早王朝城邦最現實的攻城手段，水利即攻城器械。回到基什聯盟本身，其民兵作戰仰賴城垣與城郭：一城一垣，各城自守，聯軍野戰失利時退入城內，以箭與投石消耗敵軍；這套「城邦自守加聯盟野戰」的結構，才是這場戰爭在軍事史上真正留下的東西。
tacticsEn: The method preserved by the epic is a sequence of diplomacy first, open battle second, and waterworks to close. The first step is the repeated sending of envoys: heralds travel back and forth with oral messages and with tablets, and the terms grow from barley and gemstones to gold and silver, to copper ore (kugmea), to worked metal and metalworkers, to worked stone and stonemasons, and finally to the moulds; the Arattan side stalls and at the same time offers alternatives, converting the quarrel from one of submission into one of exchange. The second step is the resort to force: Uruk and its allies mass a great host, move east over the Zubi mountains and through Anshan, and take up position on the alluvial plain on the road to Aratta; the epic describes the opposing army of Aratta as arrayed like scorpions and like birds, with strangeness of dress, the point being to convey the alien and the alarming character of a distant army rather than to give a formation that archaeology could restore. The third step is the decisive stroke: canals are opened so that the river water is led onto the plain and drowns the ground held by the enemy, which was the most practical form of siegecraft open to the Early Dynastic city, water serving as the siege engine. Returning to the Kish league itself, the militia fought behind walls and enclosures, one city one rampart, each city defending itself, and an allied army that lost the field in the open withdrew inside to wear the enemy down with arrows and slung stones; that structure of city self-defence combined with league warfare is the real legacy of this war in military history.
data: 可核對的數字如下，其中大部分是傳說數字而非歷史數字。《蘇美爾王表》給恩美爾卡爾在位 21,240 年，其中 1,760 年在基什、19,480 年在烏魯克——這是神話年表，不能當作年代的證據，卻說明蘇美爾人如何把「基什的王權」接到「烏魯克的王權」之前。史詩現存抄本屬新蘇美爾語時期，約公元前21世紀，母本可能更早；最完整的版本出自尼普爾學派，篇幅約五塊泥板，另有烏爾等學派的異本。行程方面，信使要越過祖比山、經蘇薩與安珊、翻「五、六、七座山」才到得了阿拉塔，這說明任何一支遠征軍都得走上一條極長的山地補給線。貢賦清單可以逐項點名：青金石、金、銀、銅礦（kugmea）、加工好的金屬與金屬匠人、加工石材與石匠，以及鑄模；另有以網裝載的大麥。兵器方面，本卡所屬的埃及長矛屬那卡達二期，即公元前3200年前後，與本條所收錄的戰爭年份屬同一工藝世代。戰爭列表只按年份收錄此役，起訖月份無從考訂，本條暫填四月，僅代表春汛後的典型出兵時節。傷亡與俘虜的數字完全沒有記錄，也不宜推補。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are set out below, and most of them are legendary rather than historical. The Sumerian King List gives Enmerkar a reign of 21,240 years, of which 1,760 years in Kish and 19,480 in Uruk; this is a mythological chronology and cannot serve as evidence of dates, but it does show how the Sumerians connected the kingship of Kish with the kingship of Uruk that came after. The surviving copies of the epic belong to the Neo-Sumerian period, about the twenty-first century BC, though the original may be older; the fullest version comes from the School of Nippur and runs to roughly five tablets, with variant versions from Ur and other schools. As to distance, the herald has to cross the Zubi mountains, pass Susa and Anshan and climb the 'five, six, seven' mountains to reach Aratta, which means that any expedition had to march a very long mountainous line of supply. The tribute can be listed item by item: lapis lazuli, gold, silver, copper ore (kugmea), worked metal and metalworkers, worked stone and stonemasons, and the moulds; and barley carried in nets. As for arms, the Egyptian spear of this card belongs to the Naqada II culture, around 3200 BC, and so to the same technical generation as the date under which this war is filed. The list of wars records the conflict by year alone; its opening and closing months cannot be established, and April is entered here only to mark the usual campaigning season after the spring floods. There is no record whatever of casualties or prisoners, and none should be reconstructed.
cause: 打起來的根由，是東面物產與通道之爭。基什聯盟掌握北巴比倫的穀物腹地，卻缺石料、缺金屬、缺青金石，而蘇美爾人的地理想像裡，這些東西都來自東方山地。埃蘭（或阿拉塔）扼住祖比山與安珊之間的隘口，離平原遠卻握有商路，於是它既是基什要伸手去取的對象，也是聯盟內部資源分配不均的根源。史詩把這一點改寫成宗教對抗：伊南娜原在阿拉塔，接受烏魯克伊南娜廟（埃克西安）落成後轉投烏魯克，恩美爾卡爾便以「女神已選了我」為出兵理由，要求阿拉塔交出寶石以供興建阿布祖神廟；阿拉塔之王則以「伊南娜也選中過我」為由拒絕，並提出以大麥換取寶石、以勇士單挑決鬥的折衷方案。僵持之所以升級成戰爭，一方面是神話理由被雙方拿來當合法性，另一方面是實際的距離——單是信使往返就要耗去數月，任何外交手段都難以長期維持。
causeEn: The root of the war lies in a contest over eastern produce and lines of communication. The Kish league held the grain heartland of northern Babylonia but lacked stone, metal and lapis lazuli, and in the Sumerian imagination of the world all of these came from the eastern mountains. Eran, or Aratta, held the defiles between the Zubi mountains and Anshan, far from the plain yet master of the trade route, so that it was at once the object Kish reached out to take and the source of the unequal distribution of resources inside the league. The epic rewrites this as a religious antagonism: Inanna belonged originally to Aratta, and after the E-ana of Uruk was completed she transferred her allegiance to Uruk, whereupon Enmerkar made the claim that the goddess had chosen him the pretext for war and demanded the gemstones of Aratta to build the temple of the Abzu; the lord of Aratta refused on the ground that Inanna had chosen him in his turn, and proposed a compromise, barley for gemstones and a duel between champions. The standoff turned into war for two reasons: mythological arguments were used on both sides as a claim to legitimacy, and the distances were real, since a single journey of the heralds took months and no diplomatic device could be maintained for long.
impact: 這場戰爭在書寫上留下的不是戰果，而是記憶的樣板。《蘇美爾王表》殘片與「恩赫伽爾銘文」各以一句提到「基什與埃蘭之爭」，把一場跨越山地的戰爭壓縮成王朝合法性的一段插曲；而《恩美爾卡爾與阿拉塔之王》把它擴寫成兩河流域文學的里程碑：它確立「東方出產寶石與金屬」的地理想像，這個想像在往後的蘇美爾、阿卡德與阿姆爾的關係裡一直沿用；它也把伊南娜的遷徙、語言的混亂與書寫的發明串在一起，於是這場戰爭成了《創世紀》巴別塔故事的來源之一。在制度上，它是基什霸權向烏魯克轉移的記憶入口：基什曾經是聯盟首腦，烏魯克後來取而代之，王表把恩美爾卡爾在兩地的在位年分列，正是把這個交接寫成一段連續的傳說。武器史的意義更樸素——它屬於銅器仍為主、戰車尚未出現的城邦時代，攻城靠水與土，野戰靠矛與斧，後來阿卡德王室的軍事變革（車兵與大量銅箭）尚未到來。
impactEn: What this war left behind in writing is not a record of results but the template of a memory. A fragment of the Sumerian King List and the inscription of En-hegal each mention the 'conflict between Kish and Eran' in a single clause, compressing a war fought across mountains into one episode in the legitimacy of a dynasty; and Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta expanded it into a landmark of Mesopotamian literature: it fixed the geographic imagination in which the east produces gemstones and metal, an idea that ran on through later Sumerian, Akkadian and Amorite relations; and it tied together the transfer of Inanna, the confusion of tongues and the invention of writing, so that this war became one of the sources of the Tower of Babel story in Genesis. Institutionally it is the point of entry for the memory of the transfer of hegemony from Kish to Uruk: Kish had been the head of the league, Uruk succeeded to it, and the king list, which sets down the years of Enmerkar's rule in the two places separately, writes that handover as one continuous legend. The significance for the history of arms is plainer still: this belongs to the age of the city state in which copper was still the principal metal and the war chariot had not yet arrived, siege was carried by water and earth, open battle by spear and axe, and the military reforms of the Akkadian royal house, with chariot troops and masses of copper arrowheads, were still in the future.
result: 結果分三層。史詩層面：恩美爾卡爾取得決定性的勝利，阿拉塔一方交出寶石、加工金屬、石料與工匠，並被要求交付鑄模，恩美爾卡爾因此得以興建阿布祖神廟；史詩的收束更把後果放進文明史——語言從此「多舌」，各族的言語不再一致，並以「恩尼杜穆德祈禱文」把這一切歸於恩基的安排。王表層面：基什與埃蘭的衝突被記為已經了結的一段，恩赫伽爾作為仲裁者出現，而恩美爾卡爾在基什與在烏魯克的兩段在位年，把基什的霸權與烏魯克的接續寫在同一條線上。考古層面則什麼都沒有留下——沒有戰場、沒有名冊、沒有戰利品清單，早王朝前線的痕跡只隱約反映在聚落與城址的破壞與復原上。所以這場戰爭的「結果」只能從文學傳統中讀出：那是一場以神的名義取勝、以泥板記載的勝利，也正因為記載者是詩人而不是書記，後世才把它當傳說而不是戰史。戰爭列表因此只給它一個年份，沒有月份，也沒有雙方兵力的核數。
resultEn: The result has three layers. In the epic, Enmerkar achieves a decisive victory: Aratta gives up gemstones, worked metal, stone and craftsmen, and is called upon to hand over the moulds, so that Enmerkar can build the temple of the Abzu; the close of the poem places the consequences in the history of civilisation, for speech from then on is many-tongued and the tongues of the peoples are no longer one, and it attributes the whole business to the arrangements of Enki through the prayer of Nudimmud. In the king list, the conflict between Kish and Eran is entered as a quarrel that has been settled, En-hegal appears as the arbiter, and the two stretches of Enmerkar's reign, in Kish and in Uruk, place the hegemony of Kish and the succession of Uruk on the same line. In the archaeological record, however, nothing at all is left: there is no battlefield, no roll of names and no inventory of booty, and the traces of the Early Dynastic front survive only faintly in the destruction and the rebuilding of settlements and town sites. The result of this war can therefore only be read out of the literary tradition: it was a victory won in the name of the gods and recorded on clay, and precisely because the one who recorded it was a poet rather than a scribe, later generations took it for legend rather than for history. The list of wars accordingly gives it a year and nothing else, neither a month nor a verified count of the troops on either side.
